back: The hypothesis assumed true for the test: a single value of a population parameter, e.g. p = 0.3 or μ = 50.
What we conclude if H₀ is rejected: p > 0.3 (one-tailed), p < 0.3 (one-tailed) or p ≠ 0.3 (two-tailed).
The probability of rejecting H₀ when it is true; the size of the critical region (e.g. 5%).
The set of values of the test statistic for which H₀ is rejected; the rest is the acceptance region.
The probability, under H₀, of a result at least as extreme as the one observed. Reject H₀ if p-value < significance level (half of it per tail in a two-tailed test).
Decision about H₀ + context + non-definite wording: 'there is (in)sufficient evidence at the 5% level that …'.
'Increased'/'more than': upper tail. 'Decreased'/'less than': lower tail. 'Changed'/'different': two-tailed.
The probability of the chosen critical region under H₀; usually below the nominal level.
